question: On one fixed machine and one fixed local HTTP workload, which single architecture change, applied one factor at a time to a simple full-scan baseline, produces the largest change in peak successful throughput: a cache (A1), an index (A2), read batching (A3) or bounded concurrency (A4)?
status_label: Preprint draft, not peer-reviewed. Measured on one laptop, one synthetic workload and one server on localhost; no result transfers to production traffic or other hardware. EXP-001 and EXP-002 ran under a protocol frozen by the owner; EXP-003 and EXP-004 did not run; both are to run later after the owner sets their parameters.

experiments.title: Load-generator and measurement validation
experiments.verdict: H0 holds (the two generators agree within 10 % at every level); gate for EXP-002 passed

experiments.title: One-factor-at-a-time comparison (closed-loop concurrency sweep)
experiments.verdict: A1 and A3: H0 rejected, R > 1. A4: no meaningful effect (inside [0.95, 1.05]). A2: excluded, peak generator-limited in every block (D-012 reading, chosen by the owner). Dominance: unresolved.

assumptions.name: Machine
assumptions.value: Apple M1 Pro, 10 cores, 16 GB, macOS 15.3.1

assumptions.name: Server
assumptions.value: Python 3.12 standard library http.server and sqlite3, 127.0.0.1 only

assumptions.name: Table
assumptions.value: N = 200,000 rows, 256-byte payload, rebuilt from a fixed seed for every run

assumptions.name: Concurrency sweep
assumptions.value: c in {1, 2, 4, ..., 512}, closed loop, zero think time

assumptions.name: Window
assumptions.value: 5 s warmup and a 15 s measurement window per level

assumptions.name: Blocks
assumptions.value: 10 paired blocks, arm order randomised within each block

assumptions.name: A1 cache
assumptions.value: In-process LRU of read responses, capacity 10 % of N

assumptions.name: A4 bounded concurrency
assumptions.value: W = 8 and a queue of Q = 16; overflow returns HTTP 503

assumptions.name: Generator-limited rule
assumptions.value: Goodput above 50 % of C_gen (13959.7 rps) or generator CPU above 85 %

assumptions.name: Decision rule
assumptions.value: Bonferroni 98.75 % intervals; no meaningful effect if inside [0.95, 1.05]

assumptions.name: Idle probe
assumptions.value: System-wide CPU below 15 % over 1 s before each run

limitations: One machine, one session. All confirmatory runs were made on one laptop in one window of about three hours. The intervals describe variation between process restarts within that window, not between days, machines or operating-system states; they are narrower than a reproduction elsewhere would be.
One implementation and workload. Python standard library, SQLite 3.43.1, N = 200,000, Zipf 0.99, 2 % writes. Nothing transfers to other implementations, to production traffic or to other hardware.

The baseline decides the winners. The full-scan baseline makes the index dominant by design (AM-2) and makes batching an amortisation of scans. A baseline with an index might reorder A1, A3 and A4; this was not tested.

A2 has no confirmatory estimate. The exclusion rests on the D-012 reading, which the owner chose for A2; the exploratory ratios near 247 and 91 measure the harness ceiling or a degraded region, not the index alone.
No pairwise test in the frozen analysis. The order A3 > A1 > A4 is a ranking of point estimates in the confirmatory analysis; the pairwise intervals of section 5.5 are exploratory.
Metric dependence. The size of the A3 and A4 effects changes with the summary statistic (G*, S3, closed-loop latency bound).
A4 null is structural (section 6.1) and concerns peak goodput only.

Errors not fully diagnosed. The server logs HTTP 500 without the exception type; transport errors at c of 256 and above are unclassified. The confirmatory runs validate every read body but do not re-check the final database state; write correctness rests on the pre-run tests.
Re-attempted cells. Seven cells of blocks 8 and 9 ran at the end of the sequence, paired by request sequence but not in time; leaving them out changes no verdict (X5).
Unrun sensitivity experiments. EXP-003 and EXP-004 did not run (sections 5.3 and 5.4).
Shared CPU and scheduler. Generator and server share the cores; the placement on performance or efficiency cores is not controllable.
Pilot effect sizes were visible before EXP-002. The pre-stated rule did not use them, and the analysis was committed before EXP-002 output (C4 disclosure in the freeze record).

Post hoc exploratory checks. The checks X1 to X13 were chosen at M4, after the confirmatory results were known; X12 in particular was added after the per-level latencies had been inspected. They are hypothesis-generating only.
AI assistance. The analysis readings of D-012 and every exploratory check were written by an AI assistant; they are internal quality control, not independent review.

pending_owner_decisions.title: The reading of the frozen generator-limited rule that excludes the index arm (A2)

readings.label: Owner's choice: frozen-rule reading as applied (D-012)
readings.text: A run's G* is undefined when its peak level is generator-limited, and an arm enters the comparison only if G* is defined in every block. A2 then has no confirmatory estimate and the dominance question is unresolved.

readings.label: Exploratory alternatives the manuscript reports beside it (not verdicts)
readings.text: Both place A2 far above every other arm, and both measure A2 against a ceiling or in a region that the frozen design did not intend as its peak.
